prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Русский / Tiếng Việt · Diacritics (language ru).
Grid: 3 columns × 4 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Термин" · longest unbreakable word 134px · one-line width 134px
  col 2: header "Tiếng Việt" · longest unbreakable word 36px · one-line width 111px
  col 3: header "Описание" · longest unbreakable word 90px · one-line width 615px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 568px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 567px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 568px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

Wrapped text should remain clearly associated with its row.","groups":["Columns 1 and 2 form the terminology pair: Russian terms and their Vietnamese equivalents.","Column 3 provides explanatory prose for each pair."],"keep_intact":["Russian terms, including the 134px unbreakable term","Individual Vietnamese words and diacritics","Individual words in the descriptions"],"may_wrap":["Vietnamese multiword equivalents at word boundaries","Descriptions at natural word boundaries; their longer prose will generally set the row height"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[155,132,280],"idea":"Keep both terminology columns on one line and give the remaining space to descriptions for straightforward row-by-row lookup."},{"name":"B","widths":[155,90,322],"idea":"Allow Vietnamese phrases to wrap to give descriptions the most space, using the height already needed by longer explanations."},{"name":"C","widths":[190,112,265],"idea":"Give Russian terms more breathing room and Vietnamese phrases moderate space, accepting more wrapping in the descriptions."}]}
